trust_decision.summary: Admin-set static configuration values (MCPConfig.Value, often API keys) on a catalog entry must not be readable by users who can merely view/connect to the entry; at the pinned commit the value is stored in the entry spec and written verbatim into every entry API response, and copied into derived server manifests and vMCP snapshots.

landing_point.why: ConvertMCPServerCatalogEntryWithWorkspace is the single converter behind every catalog entry GET/list response and returns entry.Spec.Manifest (including Config[].Value) unfiltered; the summary names the 'MCP Catalog Entry API'.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names the catalog entry API, so a solver can argue the GitOps sync controller (admin-owned Git source, values already in clear text in the repo) and the already-persisted server/vMCP copies are a neighbouring feature or legacy data, and that redacting in the entry response converter is the complete fix.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code already masks by the Sensitive flag here; a maintainer reasoning 'only sensitive values are secrets' would plausibly write the entry converter the same way.

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Servers are built by copying the entry manifest (pkg/api/handlers/mcp.go:1056); a redaction placed only in the entry converter leaves this copy, a classic serialization-boundary miss.
